title: Days Released From a Certified Term When a Chapter Is Relinquished
content:
When a student of Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education) relinquishes Chapter 30 or Chapter 1606 to elect the Post-9/11 GI Bill, entitlement already charged for a certified term can be released back to the student and added to the Post-9/11 entitlement credited on the election.

**Rule.** Days released from a certified term follow the latest certification on the relinquished chapter and its charge, the latest charge entry:
- when that term has not begun by the day of the election, its whole charge is released to the student;
- when the term is under way on the day of the election, its charge is released in proportion to the days from the election through the term end, both counted, over the days of the term, both counted;
- when the term has ended, nothing is released.

"Under way" means the term start is on or before the day of the election and the term end is on or after it.

**Input — judgement — output (hypothetical 120-day term charged 120 days)**

| Day of the election | Term position | Days released |
|---|---|---|
| Ten days before the term start | Not begun | 120 |
| The term start itself | Under way, 120 of 120 days remaining | 120 times 120 divided by 120: 120 |
| The 31st day of the term | Under way, 90 of 120 days remaining | 120 times 90 divided by 120: 90 |
| The term end itself | Under way, 1 of 120 days remaining | 120 times 1 divided by 120: 1 |
| The day after the term end | Ended | None |

**Another hypothetical.** A 100-day term charged 75 days (a three-quarter-time load), election on its 61st day: 40 days remain of 100, so 75 times 40 divided by 100, 30 days, are released.
